headline: Seven majors above their 200-day lines, and the crowd is greedy while momentum quietly cools
paragraphs: Start with the regime, because it's unambiguous today: all seven majors on this board, BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, BNB, DOGE, and ADA, sit above their 200-day moving averages, and four of them (ETH, SOL, BNB, and, notably, not BTC) show a golden cross. That's a market in an established uptrend, not a tentative one. Bitcoin itself trades at $80,205.69, still 35.7% below its 12-month high of $124,739.81, a reminder that 'above the 200-day' and 'near the highs' are different claims entirely.

But trend and momentum are starting to disagree, and that disagreement is the first real finding. Bitcoin's RSI-14 sits at 67.3, ETH at 66.1, SOL at 67.5, all comfortably warm without being overbought extremes, yet none of the three shows MACD above signal. That's a classic quiet divergence: price and moving averages still constructive, momentum oscillators elevated but the trend-following MACD not confirming fresh strength. BNB, DOGE, and ADA, by contrast, do have MACD above signal, so the accelerating cohort and the resting cohort aren't the same names. On the day, BTC is down 0.1%, SOL down 0.2%, and BNB down 0.1%, while the week tells a different story entirely, BTC up 3.1%, BNB up 8.8%, SOL up 2.0%. Zoom to 30 days and every asset here is up between 22% and 39%. Three different windows, three different pictures: this is a market resting within an uptrend, not reversing one.

Positioning adds texture rather than alarm. BTC funding on OKX is slightly negative at -0.4% annualized, meaning shorts are technically paying longs to hold their bets, an unusual tilt for an asset above its 200-day. ETH funding runs positive at 6.8% annualized, XRP hotter still at 10.4%, and DOGE's long/short ratio of 3.65 alongside XRP's 2.5 shows crowds leaning long on the smaller names even as BTC's book stays closer to balanced (1.08). The liquidation windows back this up: BTC saw $813,210 in short liquidations against just $3,305 in longs over the last hour, and ETH's hour shows $735,271 in shorts wiped out versus $18,266 in longs. Shorts are the ones getting run over intraday, consistent with a market that keeps grinding rather than crashing.

Flows are where the tension sharpens. BTC spot ETFs posted a net inflow of $174.6M on Sep 4, extending to a $986.7M net inflow over the last five sessions with three same-direction days, a real traditional-finance bid. ETH ETFs added $25.9M on the same day, $215.3M over five sessions. Whale exchange flows for BTC over the last 48 hours show $99.6M net moving off exchanges (154.6M out, 55.0M in), and the weekly series confirms a shift: three straight weeks of money moving onto exchanges (Aug 17 at -$441M, Aug 24 at -$946M, Aug 31 at -$775M) just flipped to $494M moving off exchanges in the week ending Sep 7. That's a fresh reversal, one week old, not yet a trend to lean on. Stablecoin float sits at $310.6B, up 1.46% over 30 days, dry powder building slowly rather than surging.

Sentiment is where the story gets its edge. Fear & Greed reads 71, Greed, near the top of its own 30-day range of 27 to 74. The crowd feels good. The tape mostly agrees, ETF inflows are real, whales are pulling BTC off exchanges this week, shorts are the ones getting liquidated. But bitcoin's own MACD sitting below signal while RSI reads 67 is the one place greed and momentum aren't fully shaking hands, a market that has run hard on the month (BTC up 22.7%) without a fresh trend-following confirmation on the daily.

What to watch: whether BTC's MACD crosses back above signal, which would resolve today's momentum-versus-trend divergence one way or the other. Watch whether the whale flow's one-week reversal to off-exchange movement extends into a second week, given three prior weeks ran the opposite direction. And watch funding: BTC's negative funding alongside positive funding on ETH, XRP, and DOGE is an uneven setup worth tracking if any of those funding rates flip sign.
